parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
**Important information for this question**
- In this question (pr) means 'a solution in propanone'.
- Sodium iodide is soluble in propanone giving $\text{Na}^+\text{(pr)}$ and $\text{I}^-\text{(pr)}$.
- Sodium chloride is insoluble in propanone.

The reaction between 2-chlorobutane and sodium iodide in propanone is shown.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHClCH}_3\text{(pr)} + \text{Na}^+\text{(pr)} + \text{I}^-\text{(pr)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHICH}_3\text{(pr)} + \text{NaCl(s)}$$

The rate of this reaction can be investigated by measuring the electrical conductivity of the reaction mixture. The electrical conductivity changes as the reaction progresses due to the precipitation of the $\text{NaCl}$ produced.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Suggest how the electrical conductivity will change as the reaction proceeds. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Describe a suitable method for studying the rate of this reaction at a temperature of $40^{\circ}\text{C}$, using the following.

- an electrical conductance meter which measures the electrical conductivity of solutions
- solutions of known concentrations of 2-chlorobutane in propanone and sodium iodide in propanone
- stopclock
- access to standard laboratory equipment

parts.label: (c)(ii)

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the relative rate for experiment 4.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Suggest the mechanism for the reaction of 2-chlorobutane with iodide ions. Draw out the steps involved, including the following.

- all relevant lone pairs and dipoles
- curly arrows to show the movement of electron pairs
- the structure of any transition state or intermediate

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
This reaction was carried out using a single optical isomer of 2-chlorobutane.

Use your mechanism in (i) to predict whether the product will be a single optical isomer or a mixture of two optical isomers. Explain your answer.
